Orwell. This experience is simply mind blowing.. the ideas and the way this game executes the plausibly realistic scenario of an indiscriminate cyber investigation system being utilised by "investigators" to obtain information on suspects who have been identified to have possible intent to harm "the Nation", legally, or more often then not; illegally.

Not many games have provided me with such a thought exercise and even less have made a lasting impression on me, and this game certainly has done exactly that. This development studio have outdone themselves immensely and I do find myself some regret of obtaining this game freely instead of supporting the developers and obtaining the game myself personally.

Orwell, has an amazing soundtrack, realistic characters (even when they did not have actual voices or anything other than their words and pictures, they felt as real to me as any other) intense story, realistic scenarios and relatable events (such as terrorist attacks, online privacy worries, etc.) I even felt a deep connection with the "advisors" to Orwell in a professional sense, especially the first one who I enjoyed his humour and his concern for things.

When I first started Orwell, I did not expect much seeing as I had jumped right into it without any thought. But after playing through Orwell for the first time, it really does make you think about things and that is the magical effect of Orwell.

"But, be warned, the information you supply will have consequences." DO not underestimate these words in the description.

Every chunk of information matters, whether it leads to leads to something more, whether it leads to social breakdown or whether it leads to disaster. 

Getting the information wrong, is not tolerable in Orwell.

100% recommend this game. Although it does not have anymore than around 5 hours of content, those 5 hours will be the most intense and enjoyable experience you will discover. Perhaps in the future this scenario will become a reality? Who knows? There is already the familiar CCTV and technology is rapidly advancing.

I wish I could give a middle ground recommendation. Story based game, little gameplay, not a bad thing but parts of the story and the execution are a little wonky. The game revolves around you uploading datachunks as they call them to a system for a detective like person, known as an Adviser, to review, these are highlighted pieces of text that maybe useful information, which is the first big problem. Rarely are these datachunks useless information so 90% of the time is ok to just upload the regular "blue" datachunks and at least half of the 10% remaining are incredibly obviously useless or incorrect, although uploading them allow you to see more "related documents" Conflicting datachunks are yellow, tell you and point to their conflicting datachunk where you generally have to make a choice which is correct, and you'll be able to find the information to make the most informed call almost every time. Quite often when uploading a datachunk it will only provide a bit of a picture from the actual uploaded text or picture but the adviser will add significantly more detail to advance the plot than the piece of information should be providing. I'm going to talk very generally about the end, no character names, examples or spoilers. Another wonky component was the final day, each day is the next episode, entering the final day the rules change and you can only upload 20 datachunks, which is a great mechanic and should've been a mechanic the whole way through the game, the reasoning for this change is really awkward because "something, fairly tame" is going to happen at a certain time during the final day, but this was not a concern elsewhere in the game. The final day brings me to the biggest problem with the game, there is a point after uploading the 20 datachunks which kind of transitions the game into the endgame portion, but during this information was revealed that I didn't know and was prevented as if I had found it, which made me feel like the entire sequence isn't heavily effected by the uploaded datachunks, it made the endgame feel very cheap as you start making what should be the very impactful decisions. You basically just select one of the endgame directions after the transition rather than all or most of your game decisions meaning something. The other problem is the ending seems extremely preachy rather than allowing the player to figure out how they feel about the subject matter.

But whats good about Orwell? The characters in general feel much more realistic rather than when you see someone try to write internet conversations and forum posts. Orwell does a pretty good job of leading and misleading you at different points which does make it more interesting. The pacing in phone calls/text chats feel really good and suspenseful, assuming the player can read fast enough to keep up, same goes for connecting documents, although some can feel way too convenient. The concept and questions it should be asking the player about the extent of security and surveillance is excellent.

Would I buy this game for $10? Probably not, it only took 5 hours to complete, including when I walked away for a few minutes. Sale price? Yah its definitely worth checking out. If its under $3 definitely get it, its an interesting ride.

My only negative point would be that the game has a medium to low replay value, as is the norm with all narrative-driven games. Although it is a bit higher than average.

Outside of that, it really is a great game full of choices, consequences, and most-importantly for me: clarity of choice. You see, the game will explicitly spell the information that is derived from the clue that you have before you. This way, there is no room for a gap between what you thought your choice would convey, and what it actually conveys. (NOTE: This doesn't preclude other characters from seeing the information through their own lens and biaises)

The theme is obviously very interesting, and the game seems to be doing a decent job at letting you form your own real-life opinions on the topic. The investigation mechanics are detailed enough that it doesn't feel like the game is railroading you, but not loose enough that you can get 'suck' or 'lost' for too long, which I really appreciate.

Overall, I'd strongly recommend the game if you are willing to explore themes that make you think about real-life ideas and ethical dillemas, wrapped into a good investigation game.

This game makes you think and decide on your own morals and act on how you deem is the best.

The Game is best described as an interactive crime novel rather than a full game.

[Pros]
It is well designed and the interaction is very streamlined and has a nice flow to it, combining the feeling of going through files like an actual investigator without the boring drawback of having 500 duds for every lead. IMO the devs nailed the ratio of work/reward in a way that is engaging, story driving and entangling.

The plot is interesting and apparently it has multiple endings with yet again multiple outcomes, it is by no means a "choose your own adventure" but it brings in just enough individuality that a second and even thrid run of the game could be interesting even if you already know the plot.

There are always multiple ways to get them juicy Data chunks you're looking for.

[Cons]

The game does a pretty good job at highlighting important information, be it in form of Data Chunks or in plain text. However oftentimes you find yourself in a spot where you discover information about a person you know has some sort of realationship with one of your POIs. However the game does not let you add said information to their profile which to me came as an enormous break in the flow.  As in: "This person seems to play a pivotal role and I have information about them that might come in handy later, why in the lords name am I not allowed to add this information?" [spoiler] Although this has happened to me a few times I most often encountered this with the lawyer, Joseph if im not mistaken, he is an important character early on yet the game does not let you collect data on him from the get go [/spoiler]
To me it felt like the game does not reward you if you are being extra thorough, which can be very discouraging.

Maybe I have not been thorough enough, but the game has major plotholes, the most annoying to me being the algorythm of Orwell knowing two data chunks are conflictive. How does the programm know that? And if it found such intricate information out without me going over it why am I needed? This could have been solved much more elegantly by having to chose which of the two statements is true; As in "her favourite colour appears to be red but in a previous statement we have assest that it is indeed blue. Do you wish to edit your previous assesment or keep the original?". This could have also gven us more opportunity to bond with our evaluator, whom I have perceived as rather robotic since he basically only shows emotions when you make mistakes. [spoiler] Honestly the big J plottwist was such an anticlimactic ending, although I understand her "motivations" I do not understand how harrison fits in the picture. The life insurance was for his mother ofc. But did he also fake correspondance as Abraham? How does that fit in? Why did we not find any indication of this earlier? It felt like a very cheap reveal alà modern sherlock holmes, where the pieces just happen to fall in a way nobody could have predicted and resolving the story in a very dry and undercut way. How did they manage to find out initiate's number? Why dont we have access to that if they can just, hypothetically, recall? [/spoiler] This way of resolving the main plot does not do their way of engaging storytelling justice in the slightest. 

[Verdict]

A very different approach to the interactive novel, I enjoyed it altough it has some shorcomings. The way the game involves the player and tells it's story is superb and deserves a better plot than what we are given.

Good game on what it's like to be big brother spying on citizens and trying to solve a terror plot. Has a lot of implications to our current situation.

Pros
Good story, believable characters.
The interface to spy and upload information on the various people you spy on was done well. It does feel like you're working for a big government entity.
Decisions you make on what information to report does matter.

Cons
Certain aspects of the story regarding a few of the character could be a little bit more flushed out.
Not a big fan of the art style but that's a personal perference

Buy it if you have a chance.
